`mesh()` checks every tetrahedron against a quality threshold (0.01 by
default) and, with the default `FeatureRecipe()` or any other recipe that
enforces the threshold, delivers no mesh that fails it; the report it writes in
the run's `mesh/` folder says what it found. `GmshDefaultRecipe` is the
exception: it records the quality without enforcing the threshold. This page explains the measure, shows a real
report, and lists what the report and the mesh summary record.
[Inspect the prepared model](../../guides/inspect-the-prepared-model.qmd) shows
where to look before you run a solver.

## What `mesh()` checks {#audit}

The measure is the minimum signed inverse condition number, **minSICN**, of
each tetrahedron. It is 1 for a regular tetrahedron, falls towards 0 as the
element flattens, and is negative for an inverted one. Every tetrahedron must
reach `quality_threshold`, 0.01 unless you set another with `set_mesh`. For
scale: the real report below has a lowest minSICN of 0.04212; in the
[band-boundary measurement](palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#palace-mesh-band-edges)
delivered meshes reached 0.08 to 0.23 with the multiple 2 and 0.014 to 0.019
on the pad with the multiple 8, while a mesh that stalled held elements of
0.003 to 0.004.

With `FeatureRecipe`, `GlobalSizeRecipe` or `UniformBoundaryRecipe`, elements
below the threshold are refined in the next repair round, within the
[budgets](palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#palace-mesh-controls), and a mesh that
cannot be brought up to the threshold stops `mesh()`: no `palace.msh` is
delivered. `set_mesh(recipe=GmshDefaultRecipe())` meshes once without repair
and delivers the mesh whatever its quality; the report still records the
minSICN and the tetrahedra below the threshold, and its `stop` is
`report_only` when there are any. The check is made on the linear mesh,
before any raising to the geometry order.

A mesh that passes is a mesh of valid elements, not a converged result:
convergence is read from the solver's passes
([the convergence declaration](palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#convergence-declaration)).

## The quality report {#quality-report}

Each run writes the report to `mesh/` as JSON (`<model>.quality.json`) and as a
short text (`<model>.quality.txt`). This is the text of a real report:
SCGSim's test model of a 20 µm pad in a 40 µm ground cutout on a 100 µm die,
Route B with MA, MS and SA bands at 0.5 and 1.0 µm, meshed by the meshing
module with Gmsh 4.15.2 and the default settings:

```text
scgsim.meshing scgsim.meshing.features/3: clean after 0 refinement rounds
  quality measure minSICN, threshold 0.01
  19722 tetrahedra, min quality 0.04212, 0 below the threshold (linear mesh before elevation); algorithm 1, geometry order 1
  143 sized curves, 0 local sizes, smallest -
  total 1.7 s; limit 180 s, target 60 s for 0.0196 mm2
```

Read the first three lines first: how the repair ended (`clean`, or the stop
reason), the lowest quality, and how many elements are below the threshold.
The JSON holds the full record:

::: {.askr-table-compact}
| Field | Records |
|---|---|
| `quality_measure`, `threshold` | `minSICN` and the threshold the run was held to. |
| `stop`, `rounds`, `history` | How the repair ended and what each round changed. |
| `mesh` | Tetrahedron and node counts, `min_quality`, `bad_count` below the threshold, `measured_on` (`linear mesh before elevation`), the delivered `geometry_order` and the 3D algorithm. `null` when no round made a mesh. |
| `meshing_stage` | Every finding of the meshing-stage check, with the limits it used, as `simulation_drc` reports them. `null` for a delivered mesh. |
| `remaining_bad`, `stop_places` | The elements still below the threshold, with their place, groups and feature kinds, and where they cluster, with the fine edges or faces found there. Empty for a clean stop. |
| `recipe`, `repair`, `mesher`, `budgets`, `time_budget` | The settings the run used. |
| `timing` | Total, per-round, meshing and check seconds, kept under one key so that two runs of the same input compare equal without it. |
:::

The mesh manifest records the report's path and SHA-256, the order of the
written mesh and its element types. The report says nothing about curved
high-order elements, since it measures the linear mesh.

## Edge statistics {#edge-statistics}

The [mesh summary](palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#mesh-manifest-and-detached-summary)
gives each physical region's number of edges and the shortest, mean and
longest edge length in micrometres, measured as straight chords between corner
nodes, also on curved elements.

## Telling two meshes apart {#version-identities}

A mesh carries three versions; compare them to tell whether two meshes were
made the same way.

::: {.askr-table-compact}
| Identity | Example | Where it is recorded | Changes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Package version | `scgsim <version>` | `scgsim_version` in the run's provenance (`metadata/route_b_provenance.json`, or `route_a_…` on Route A) | With every release of SCGSim |
| Recipe version | `scgsim.meshing.features/3` for `FeatureRecipe`; `uniform-boundary/N`, `global-size/N` for the others | `recipe.version` in each quality report and in the mesh manifest, beside `recipe.parameters` | Only when the sizes the recipe asks for change |
| Report format | `scgsim.meshing.report/N` | `report_version` in each quality report | When the report's fields change |
:::

Two reports with the same recipe version and the same parameters asked for the
same starting sizes, even from different SCGSim releases; a different recipe
version means different sizing rules. The repair settings are in each report
and the Gmsh version in the mesh manifest. Why the versions are kept apart,
with a measured example of two recipe versions, is in
[the internals](../../contribute/internals/report-records.qmd#mesh-version-identities).
